steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: Who's there?
Excuse me, we're just passing mercenaries. The rain's getting heavy, so we'd like to shelter here for a while. Would that be alright?

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: You can head on over to the village inn.
We'll only be here until the rain clears up. We can't stay long anyway.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: Anyone else with you?
Just my friend. She can't walk very well.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: Sarkaz?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We mean you no harm.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: Your kind isn't welcome here, devil. Get lost.
A longsword is pointed at her neck.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: I'm not gonna repeat myself.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Then, please... at least allow my friend to rest here.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: What's her problem?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: The same as you, good sir.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: Infected?

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: You said you're a merc, yeah?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: Stay right here by the door, and don't go wandering off.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Dad, do we have guests?

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: Nothing you need to worry about. Head back inside.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Okay...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Ngh...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: You're awake, Liz?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We were fortunate enough to find a place to rest. It won't be much longer until we're out of Victoria.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Thank goodness...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: You make sure to get some rest too, alright?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Thank you. I'll do just that.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Ma'am, do you need a towel?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Thank you very much.
From afar, the owner of the home watches his daughter approach the Sarkaz, and he reaches subconsciously for the hilt of his sword.
But what he'd feared did not come to pass.
Shining accepts the towel and helps Nightingale dry her hair. After painstakingly tending to her companion, she then wipes down her own long, dripping hair.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Did you need anything else?

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: N-No, I was just thinking of something to say...
Chirp, chirp.
A small blue creature pops out from Nightingale's pocket and lands on her shoulder.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Whoa, a fowlbeast!

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Can I pet it?!

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Mhm.
Nightingale raises her hand, and the fowlbeast hops from her shoulder to her fingertips.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: I've never seen such an obedient fowlbeast before!

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Heehee~ Hello there~

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Where are you from?
The fowlbeast chirps, as if replying to the girl's question.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Little fowlbeast, little fowlbeast, do you want to play a game?

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: My dad made me a lot of toys, but the other kids in the village don't like playing with me.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Game? What kind of game?

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Do you wanna play too, ma'am?! Give me a sec!
The girl hurries back into her room to search for something.
After rummaging around for a while, she comes back with a small cardboard box.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: I have a lot of really fun stuff. My dad carved them all out of wood!

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: My favorite is this one—

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Huh...
The girl digs through the box, pulling out a wooden block or two every now and then.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Everything's fallen apart...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Is there anything I can help you with?

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Oh, yes, thanks.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Can you help me take all the blocks out? Then stack them up in groups of three. First horizontally, then vertically, and repeat.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Alright.
Shining helps the child dig through the box and pick out all the wooden blocks.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Your horns are so beautiful! Are you an Elafia?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: No, I'm a Sarkaz.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Oh, that makes sense... You don't have those fluffy ear tufts.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: I heard you're gonna leave Victoria after this when I was in my room.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Is Victoria... bad?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: No, it's just...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: This country isn't for us.
Shining picks up some of the wooden blocks she had dug out from the box and begins stacking them on top of one another.
After only a few layers, the colors before her eyes already seem to be coalescing into a kaleidoscopic blur.
It has been a long time since she's experienced an environment so replete with warmth. As she relaxes, drowsiness starts to wash over her.
Her thoughts spin through the air along with motes of light.
Shining can already see the light coming from the exit.
And behind her, piled high in the shadows, are the bodies of Confessarius guards.
She simply pats the person strapped to her back — and does not turn around.
Nightingale is still not fully awake, and subconsciously clings tight to Shining.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Hang in there a bit longer, Liz.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: There they are!

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We need to leave this place.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: ...Though to where, I couldn't say either.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: There may be no place for us in these lands.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: But at the very least...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: I refuse to leave you behind here.
The daylight flashes by from within the cave, leaving its vestiges on the supporting pillars and rocks.
Before Shining emerges, a blue fowlbeast has already darted out, flying impatiently towards the sunlight.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard A
steps.text: That sound just now — did it come from over there?

steps.name: Confessarius Guard B
steps.text: That's where they fled to.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard B
steps.text: I'll give chase. You report to the leader.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard A
steps.text: What's going on?

steps.name: Confessarius Guard B
steps.text: The cave entrance is about to collapse! Retreat, now!

steps.name: Confessarius Guard A
steps.text: W-We won't make it in time—!!
Owwww!
A yelp suddenly snaps Shining back to reality.
The girl had accidentally knocked over the nearly-completed tower of wooden blocks, sending the pieces scattering everywhere.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: You're not going to rest a little more?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: I'll manage.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Ugh... Now I have to start all over again.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: There's nothing wrong with starting over.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Can I... help too this time?

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Yeah, of course! The more the merrier!
As the three of them start rebuilding the tower, Shining glances over at the owner of the house.
He is seated by the window, longsword still in hand.
Meanwhile, his child is sitting with the two women, pushing some of the fallen blocks in front of Nightingale before continuing to stack them up.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: One more... to go... And, done!

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: We can start playing the game now!

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: The rules are really easy. First, you roll the dice, then you pull out the same number of blocks from the tower and stack them on top. Whoever knocks it over loses!

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Let's roll the dice to see who goes first.
The die bounces several times under their gaze before coming to a decision.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I'm going first then?

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Yup!
Nightingale picks up the die and lets it roll off her palm.
She can't muster much strength, but it's okay since this is the first block.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: You're up next, nice lady in black.
Shining takes the die next and casts it.
She takes note of the number, and turns to the wooden tower.
While removing a block isn't inherently difficult, the tower will naturally start falling apart as the game progresses.
Past choices and occurrences accumulate, stacking up layer by layer, and applying ever more pressure on the future.
A sensation she finds disagreeable.
But rules are rules, and she must abide by them.
And so, another block is stacked on top.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Phew... How are you feeling, Liz?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Mm... No issues here...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We're already quite far from the lab. It's not likely that they'd catch up to us at this point.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We still have a long way to go. Let's get some rest and have a bite to eat.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I'm not hungry yet...
Shining opens her bag and finds she has only one piece of fruit left.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We only have a bit of dry food left. Can you eat the fruit first?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: There should be a village just across the bridge where I can buy us some food.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Here, go ahead and eat. I've peeled it for you.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Thank you...
As soon as they step into the village, they are surrounded by a constant chorus of surprised murmurs, as if they were beasts that had broken loose.
But Shining doesn't care about that. The Victorians won't see them again after they're done buying food.

steps.name: Bread Vendor
steps.text: Hello, can I help you...

steps.name: Bread Vendor
steps.text: D-Devils?!

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Good day. I'd like to purchase some bread.

steps.name: Bread Vendor
steps.text: Away with you! I don't do business with devils!

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Just name your price. I'll pay.

steps.name: Bread Vendor
steps.text: Hah. If I accepted your money, who'd still eat my bread?

steps.name: Bread Vendor
steps.text: Now scram. There are customers behind you.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: My apologies.
Shining's hand presses into the hilt of her sword.
The morning light flashes by.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Bread Vendor
steps.text: Eeeek!

steps.name: Bread Vendor
steps.text: M-Murderer!

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Wait—
Shining had long since noticed the Confessarius guards tailing her, so she had deliberately been avoiding crowded places to keep a low profile.
But as the bread stall owner runs towards the crowd, yelling and shrieking, more and more people start to gather.
'That devil's a murderer!'
'Someone get the police!'
'Isn't the village chief's son a caster? Hurry and get him over here!'
She only wanted to buy some food to fill her stomach, but she has no choice but to hastily flee the village in the end.
Her companion can only clutch fearfully at her robe, trembling uncontrollably.
And even further behind them, screams and curses continue for a long while.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Shining?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Hmm?
When she focuses on the present again, the three of them had already been playing together for quite some time.
Several of the wooden tower levels are supported by only a single block, yet the rickety tower somehow still maintains an uneasy equilibrium.
It won't be long until a winner is decided.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Is there anything I can help you with?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I think... I can do this.
The block she grabs is wedged so tightly that all blocks above it wobble every time Nightingale tries to move it.
Nightingale and the child continue staring intently at the block, neither noticing that Shining and the owner of the house have stood up at the same time.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: I think I left my wallet outside.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Would you mind keeping an eye on my friend? I'll be right back.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: It's nothing. Let's continue.
She tries again and again, hoping that the tower's center of gravity might change.
But the pressure exerted on that single block of wood does not let up.
What would Shining do? She ponders.
She remembers that Shining would draw out the blocks faster than the eye can see, without giving the tower even a chance to wobble.
She prepares to give it a try.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: You can do it!

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Mhm.
Nightingale takes a deep breath, grabs the wooden block, and forcefully pulls—
The morning light outside the window disappears in an instant as the tower collapses.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Yay! I win!
For whatever reason, the young girl takes Nightingale's hand and starts dancing around, as if they had both won the game.
Her pure, genuine emotions send a ripple through Nightingale's stony heart.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: You're back.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: I saw everything. One flick of your sword, and...

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: Are you two on the run too?
Shining looks out the window. The rain gradually subsides, and the deepening darkness serves well to conceal the corpses.
Eight Confessarius guards, and six assassins of unknown origin. Two different groups had arrived at the same doorstep.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: So, the other group of six—

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: Came to kill my child.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Is that why you were willing to shelter us from the rain?

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: It's because... you're Sarkaz.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: It was a race against time. And the guard I hired hasn't gotten here yet.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: You two are Sarkaz, and I know for a fact that that hoity-toity noble would never deign to hire one.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: You seemed capable, so I decided to hedge my bets. But I never thought you'd...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: It's fine. I understand.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: In any case, you've done me a huge favor. If you're in no hurry to leave, feel free to stay the night.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Thank you, sir. We truly appreciate your kind offer, but unfortunately time is not on our side either.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: One sec.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: It'll be tough for you to buy food along the way, right? Here, I have some bread and jerky.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: This is... Thank you very much, sir.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: I should be thanking you, Sarkaz.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: I haven't seen my daughter having this much fun with others in a long, long time.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: She's been like this since she was little. Never suspicious towards anyone.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: But we've always been on the run. Constantly moving, avoiding others. She hasn't had much of a chance to have normal interactions.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: But those days will soon be over. Once that merc shows up and takes her to live with her relatives, she'll finally be able to settle down.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: You're not going with her?

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: That damn noble killed my wife and got me sick... Once my daughter's out of harm's way, I'm getting payback, one way or another.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: I won't run.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: The rain's stopped.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Once again, thank you for letting us stay. We must be on our way now.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz, it's time to go.

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: It's already so late, though. Are you sure you don't want to stay the night?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: I'm sorry. We'll come play with you again if we get the chance, okay?

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Okay...

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Wait!

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Here, this is for you!
The girl stuffs two rocks into Shining's hand.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: What are these?

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: They're two lucky rocks I found by the river!

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Lucky... rocks?

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Yeah! Just tap them together, and you'll be sure to have good luck!

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: The last time I did it, Dad brought home a huge fowlbeast and we had a big feast!

steps.name: Villager's Child
steps.text: Maybe the next time you tap them, we'll be able to meet again!

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: I hope that day comes as well.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: Farewell, Sarkaz. Until we meet again.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Until we meet again.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: You're finally here?
Hello, Mr. Edmund.

steps.name: Infected Villager
steps.text: Thanks for coming all the way out here, Ms. Nearl. Please, come in.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: This lucky rock is for you.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Huh...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Were you happy?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: ...not sure I understand what that means.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: But, I did feel... very warm...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Being cared for, being appreciated...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Seeing someone offer a helping hand, and being able to hold it... instead of having a sword pointed at you.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: If we could always have opportunities like these... I'm sure... I'd be happy.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Can we try stopping by the village again, some other time?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Not everyone will treat us with kindness.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We're Sarkaz, and infected with Oripathy. Most in this land will not welcome us.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Had that homeowner not also been an Infected, we might not even have had the opportunity to rest beneath those eaves.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: But, there's always a chance, right?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Sometimes, we can relieve the suffering of others. So I believe that, sometimes, others can do the same for us.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Even if the likelihood is extremely slim?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I believe in you, Shining. Someone out there will recognize your sincerity, your earnestness.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: ...If you say so.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Whenever we pass by a village, I'll ask the villagers. Whenever I see a caravan, I'll ask the merchants.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: People will look down on us and ignore us. We must be prepared for that.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: But if luck is on our side, we may yet find selfless people willing to help us. And maybe, in the not-too-distant future, we may even find a place where we can finally rest our feet.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: But luck is already on our side.
Nightingale takes out the lucky rock Shining had given her.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Mm, that's right.
Shining also takes out hers.
The two rocks bump together, making a crisp, clean sound.
Beneath the moonlight, the two Sarkaz leave Victoria, blessed by luck.
